column3: The Hebrew explicitly names the house of his mother’s father; BSB condenses this to the clan of his mother.
The Hebrew says to speak “in the ears” and uses “your bone and your flesh”; BSB says “ask” and “your own flesh and blood”.
The Hebrew retains the image of speaking in their ears and uses singular “their heart”; BSB has “in the presence” and plural “hearts”.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name the weight unit “shekels” and describes the men following as a separate narrative action.
The Hebrew introduces the brothers as sons of Jerubbaal and then numbers them as seventy men; BSB attaches seventy directly to brothers.
The Hebrew repeats “all” before Beth-millo and separately narrates their going before making Abimelech king.
The Hebrew actively says “they told Jotham” and describes the mountain summit as its head.
The Hebrew emphasizes going by repeating its root; it has no explicit “one day”.
The Hebrew describes going to sway over the trees; BSB uses the idiom “hold sway over the trees”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains an image of swaying over the trees rather than the idiom “hold sway”.

The Hebrew specifies new wine and retains the image of swaying over the trees.
The Hebrew says “and” without an explicit “finally”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to the deeds of his hands; BSB condenses this to “as he deserves”.
The Hebrew retains the image of throwing away his life and makes delivering them a separate narrative action.

The Hebrew uses two flight verbs and gives Abimelech as the reason for living there without an explicit word “fear”.

The Hebrew names an evil spirit and then narrates the leaders’ treachery as their action; BSB calls it a spirit of animosity and explicitly says God caused them to act deceitfully.
The Hebrew retains images of placing their blood upon Abimelech and strengthening his hands. It explicitly calls Abimelech their brother and says he killed them.
The Hebrew says “for him” without repeating Abimelech’s name and calls the hilltops heads.
